knowledge_abstraction.bug_theme: Compiled execution mode omits input bounds validation that eager execution enforces
knowledge_abstraction.general_principle: Optimizing compilers and graph transformations may remove or omit runtime input validation that eager execution performs, causing compiled execution to return incorrect results or perform out-of-bound reads instead of raising the same API-level error.

risk_dimensions.shape: Selected dimension boundaries, small dimensions, and index values at or outside the valid range
risk_dimensions.memory: Out-of-bound reads or invalid memory access caused by missing bounds checks in compiled kernels
risk_dimensions.device: CPU and backend execution transitions between eager and compiled modes
risk_dimensions.execution_state: Compiled execution state versus eager execution state

failure_mechanism.description: Backend-generated kernels may rely on compiler optimizations that remove runtime bounds checks or do not preserve eager-mode validation semantics, causing invalid indices to be accepted and processed.

input_exploration: Explore index tensors with values at the selected dimension boundary
Explore index tensors with values just outside the valid range, including negative out-of-range values
Vary selected dimension sizes, especially small dimensions where boundary violations are easier to trigger
Test indexing-like operations under both eager execution and optimized compiled execution
constraint_awareness: Eager execution defines the expected API contract for invalid inputs
Compiled execution should preserve validation and error semantics from eager execution
Out-of-range indices are invalid and should raise an error rather than silently returning data
oracle_strategy: Use eager execution as the reference oracle for exception behavior
If eager execution raises an error for invalid input, compiled execution must also raise an error
Monitor for incorrect output values or silent out-of-bound memory access when error parity is violated

transferability.description: This knowledge applies broadly to index-selection, gather, slice, and similar data-access APIs that can be transformed by optimizing compilers. Any backend optimization that removes or reorders validation logic may break the API contract for invalid inputs, so the testing principle is not limited to torch.index_select.

important_considerations: Focus on boundary and out-of-range indices for indexing and gather-style APIs
Compare eager execution semantics with compiled or optimized execution modes
Treat eager exception behavior and output correctness as the reference contract
Consider small selected dimensions to make invalid index cases easy to surface
generation_strategy: Generate harnesses that systematically vary selected dimension sizes, index values around valid boundaries, and execution modes such as eager and optimized compiled paths. Use eager execution as the oracle and validate that compiled execution preserves both error behavior and output correctness for invalid or boundary inputs.
